intent: To validate the use of objective standards in pretrial decisions by presenting encouraging data on defendant compliance and public safety.

units.meaning: The release rate: 94% of defendants were released pretrial.

basis.note: Table value is 94; narration supplies the percent sign.

accepted_routes: about 94 out of every 100 defendants were released pretrial
units.visual_evidence_rule: A bar or label for Released Pretrial must be visible with value 94 or 94%.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause stating 94% of defendants were released pre-trial.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 94% pretrial release rate required in the final video?

units.meaning: Among released defendants, 88% returned for every court date.

basis.note: Table value is 88; narration indicates the denominator is released pretrial defendants.

accepted_routes: 88% of released defendants returned for every court date
of those released pretrial, 88% made every court date
nearly nine in ten released defendants returned for every court date
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show Returned for Every Court Date with 88 or 88% and, if possible, label it as conditional on released defendants.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause stating 88% of those returned for every single court date.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video preserve the conditional denominator 'of released defendants' for the 88% figure?

units.meaning: Among released defendants, 86% were not arrested pretrial.

basis.note: Table value is 86; narration links the no-arrest period to released defendants.

accepted_routes: 86% of released defendants were not arrested pretrial
86% were not arrested during the pretrial period
about 86% of released defendants avoided pretrial arrest
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show Not Arrested Pretrial with 86 or 86% and avoid implying it is a rate for all defendants unless stated.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause stating 86% were not arrested during that time.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video present 86% as a public-safety outcome for released defendants?

units.meaning: The displayed rates rank as Released Pretrial 94%, then Returned for Every Court Date 88%, then Not Arrested Pretrial 86%.

basis.note: Highest of the three displayed values.
Middle of the three displayed values.
Lowest of the three displayed values.

accepted_routes: 94% is the highest rate, followed by 88% and then 86%
the three bars descend from 94% to 88% to 86%
release rate ranks first, return-for-court second, and not-arrested third
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must make the descending order of the three bars or labels visible.
units.temporal_anchor: Across the three data clauses, if the video shows all three bars together.
units.reviewer_question: Should the final video be required to show the descending order, or is showing the three values enough?

units.meaning: Among released defendants, the return-for-every-court-date rate is 2 percentage points higher than the not-arrested-pretrial rate (88% minus 86%).

basis.note: Used as minuend in the derived 2-point comparison.
Used as subtrahend in the derived 2-point comparison.

accepted_routes: return rate is 2 percentage points above the not-arrested rate
compliance exceeds no-arrest by 2 percentage points
units.visual_evidence_rule: If called out, the chart must show both 88% and 86% with comparable denominators (released defendants).
units.temporal_anchor: The second and third data clauses jointly, only if both are framed as among released defendants.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 2-point difference between return-for-court and not-arrested rates worth an explicit callout?

optional_valid: The video may note that all three displayed rates are high or encouraging.
The video may show that the minimum displayed rate is 86%.
The video may use the table's relative_value fields for internal bar scaling without requiring viewers to read them.
unsupported_to_avoid: Do not claim that objective standards or any policy caused the 94%, 88%, or 86% rates.
Do not say 88% or 86% of all defendants; the narration ties these outcomes to released pretrial defendants.
Do not subtract 94% - 88% or 94% - 86% as if all three rates had the same denominator.
Do not invent total defendant counts, arrest counts, or other values not in the table.
Do not cite dates or values not present in the table as chart data unless separately sourced.
notes: Core required candidates are the three narrated rates: 94, 88, and 86, with the 88 and 86 figures conditional on released defendants. Ranking and the 88-vs-86 gap are optional but valid if denominators are handled correctly.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
